grand_strategy.reading: Burundi's grand strategy is to keep the CNDD-FDD in power, which the 2018 referendum and the 2020 election secured for the long term, and to keep the Congo war off its own soil by fighting beside Kinshasa. That alignment puts Bujumbura against the side Kigali is described as backing, so the rivalry with Rwanda now runs through the M23 war as well as through the 2015 coup accusation. The weak point is the economy, a farm-based state of about USD 6.75bn that hosts the refugees the war pushes across its border; the 2025 legislative election, the Rwanda border closure and the sanctions record are not yet verified here.

stances.note: Burundi accused Rwanda of backing the 2015 coup attempt, a charge Reuters recalled in January 2025. The two now stand on opposite sides of the M23 war: Burundi's troops fight M23 beside Kinshasa, and Al Jazeera reports Rwanda is described as backing the offensive, which Rwanda denies. Rival is our reading (C): friction and opposed interests, with no source calling it an aim to destroy the other state. Bond grievance is our reading of the 2015 accusation; trend stable, since no source shows a change. Gaps: the border closure since January 2024 and the RED-Tabara charge are not verified in this pass. Mirror: the RWA card is not written yet, so nothing is mirrored. The Reuters page was cited through Wikipedia and not opened.

stances_toward.note: Rival, not adversary. Burundi shut the border and cut ties in January 2024 over RED-Tabara, its president told the BBC in March 2025 that Rwanda planned to attack, and Burundian troops (about 20,000 on Kigali's count, with the FARDC) fight the AFC/M23-RDF coalition in South Kivu; Kigali accuses the FDNB of shelling Kamanyola (Dec 2025) and of fighting with the FDLR. Neither capital declares the other regime's end; the aim is to deny the other a proxy and a front. The UN experts (2026) say RED-Tabara and FNL fighters joined the AFC/M23-RDF side and that RED-Tabara recruited in Rwanda's Mahama camp. The Rwanda border is still shut in 2026 (the reopening of some Burundian posts on 25 Feb 2026 concerned the DRC frontier). Bond grievance: Burundi blamed Rwanda for the 2015 coup attempt (a charge Reuters recalled in Jan 2025) and the two accuse each other of sheltering rebels. Evidence mirrored from Burundi's card (same Reuters and Al Jazeera links), which grades Rwanda a rival too.
